# Behavioral Design Specification: SPI Host Core Control FSM

## 1. Overview

This module is the central control state machine for the SPI host. It receives command-segment descriptors, executes them on the SPI bus, and produces the timing and data-path control signals needed to move data to and from the SPI pins.

The module is responsible for:

- Accepting command segments from the command interface.
- Generating the serial clock with the configured polarity, phase, and divisor.
- Controlling the active-low chip-select outputs.
- Applying programmable chip-select lead, trail, and idle timing.
- Controlling the direction of the SPI data line drivers.
- Generating data-path strobes for TX byte reads, RX byte writes, bit shifting, and receive sampling.
- Pausing and holding state when the TX or RX data path is not ready.
- Supporting back-to-back command segments without deasserting chip select when requested.

## 2. Reset, Enable, and Initialization

### 2.1 Hardware Reset

On hardware reset, the module shall:

- Return to the idle state.
- Deassert all chip-select outputs.
- Stop the serial clock at its idle level.
- Disable all SPI data line drivers.
- Clear all transfer counters and status indications.
- Not accept commands.

### 2.2 Software Reset

A software reset request shall abort any in-progress transaction and return the module to the idle state. While software reset is asserted:

- No command segments shall be accepted.
- The serial clock shall not toggle.
- All chip-select outputs shall be deasserted.
- All data-path strobes shall be suppressed.

After software reset is released, the module shall behave as if it had returned to the idle state and shall be ready to accept a new command when enabled.

### 2.3 Core Enable

The module shall not advance through its states or generate serial clock edges unless the core enable input is asserted.

When the core enable is deasserted:

- The current state shall be frozen.
- The serial clock shall hold its current level.
- The chip-select outputs shall hold their current levels.
- No new command shall be acknowledged.
- No TX or RX data strobes shall be generated.

When the core enable is reasserted, operation shall resume from the exact point at which it was paused.

## 3. Command Segment Interface

### 3.1 Command Acceptance

The module shall accept a command segment when all of the following conditions are true:

- The module is ready for a new segment.
- A valid segment descriptor is presented on the command interface.
- The core is enabled.
- The module is not stalled.

A segment descriptor includes:

- The target chip-select identifier.
- The serial clock configuration: polarity, phase, clock divisor, and full-cycle mode.
- The chip-select timing configuration: lead time, trail time, and idle time.
- The segment length.
- The segment direction: TX-only, RX-only, bidirectional, or dummy.
- The segment speed: standard, dual, or quad.
- A chip-select-active-after-transfer flag.

When a segment is accepted, the module shall use the supplied configuration for that segment.

### 3.2 Ready Behavior

The module shall assert command-ready whenever it can accept a new segment.

Command-ready shall be asserted in the following situations:

- When the module is fully idle and the inter-transaction idle time has been satisfied.
- When the module is holding the chip-select output low after a segment with the chip-select-active-after-transfer flag set, and no segment is currently executing.
- At the end of an executing segment if the chip-select-active-after-transfer flag is set and the next segment for the same chip-select is already pending.

Command-ready shall not be asserted while:

- The module is stalled.
- A chip-select switch sequence is still enforcing trail or idle timing.
- A software reset is asserted.
- The core enable is deasserted.

### 3.3 Segment Types and Length Units

The module shall interpret the segment length according to the segment direction:

- For TX-only, RX-only, and bidirectional segments, the length is in bytes.
- For dummy segments, the length is in serial clock cycles.

For a data segment:

- Standard speed requires eight serial clock cycles per byte.
- Dual speed requires four serial clock cycles per byte.
- Quad speed requires two serial clock cycles per byte.

For a dummy segment, exactly one serial clock cycle is generated per unit of length, and no data is read from or written to the data path.

### 3.4 Back-to-Back Segments

When a segment has the chip-select-active-after-transfer flag set, the module shall keep the chip-select output asserted after the segment ends and wait for the next command.

If the next command is for the same chip-select identifier and is already pending when the segment ends, the module may acknowledge it immediately and begin the next segment without raising the chip-select line.

If no next command is pending, the module shall remain in a chip-select-active idle state. In this state:

- The chip-select output stays low.
- The module is considered inactive for activity-status purposes.
- Command-ready remains asserted.
- A subsequent command for the same chip-select can start immediately.
- A subsequent command for a different chip-select shall first cause the current transaction to be terminated with the required trail and idle timing.

## 4. Serial Clock Generation

### 4.1 Clock Division

The module shall generate the serial clock from the core clock using the supplied clock divisor value.

The serial clock period shall be equal to:

- Twice the core clock period times the clock divisor plus one.

Equivalently, each low phase and each high phase of the serial clock shall last for one clock-divisor interval.

A clock divisor value of zero shall produce the fastest serial clock, with a period of two core clock cycles.

The clock divider shall be aligned so that serial clock edges occur only at the boundaries of the chip-select lead, trail, and idle timing intervals.

### 4.2 Clock Polarity and Phase

The serial clock shall be held at its idle level whenever a transaction is not actively clocking data.

- If the clock polarity is zero, the idle level is low.
- If the clock polarity is one, the idle level is high.

The clock phase shall determine the relationship between data output and serial clock edges:

- With phase zero, the first bit of each byte shall be presented before the first serial clock edge of that byte. Subsequent bits shall be shifted on the opposite edge from the edge on which they are sampled.
- With phase one, the first bit of each byte shall be presented on the first serial clock edge of that byte. Data shifting shall follow the standard SPI phase-one convention.

The module shall provide data-path strobes that are consistent with the selected clock phase, so that data is driven and sampled on the correct edges.

## 5. Chip-Select Control and Transaction Timing

### 5.1 Chip-Select Mapping

The module shall support a parameterizable number of chip-select lines. Each chip-select identifier selects exactly one chip-select output.

When a segment is executed:

- The selected chip-select output shall be asserted low.
- All other chip-select outputs shall remain deasserted high.

When no transaction is active, all chip-select outputs shall be deasserted high.

### 5.2 Transaction Start Timing

When starting a transaction from the fully idle state with the chip-select line high, the module shall:

1. Assert the selected chip-select output low.
2. Wait the configured chip-select lead time.
3. Begin generating serial clock edges.

The lead time shall be measured from the falling edge of the chip-select line to the first serial clock edge.

A configured lead-time value of zero shall produce the default minimum of one half serial clock period. Each additional increment in the lead-time value shall add one half serial clock period.

### 5.3 Transaction End Timing

At the end of a segment that does not have the chip-select-active-after-transfer flag set, the module shall:

1. Stop the serial clock at its idle level.
2. Hold the chip-select output low for the configured trail time.
3. Deassert the chip-select output high.
4. Wait the configured idle time before accepting another command or asserting a chip-select again.

The trail time shall be measured from the last serial clock edge to the rising edge of the chip-select line. The idle time shall be measured from the rising edge of the chip-select line to the next chip-select assertion.

A trail-time or idle-time value of zero shall produce the default minimum of one half serial clock period. Each additional increment shall add one half serial clock period.

### 5.4 Chip-Select Hold Between Segments

When a segment has the chip-select-active-after-transfer flag set, the module shall not deassert the chip-select output at the end of the segment. Instead, it shall hold the chip-select output low and wait for the next segment.

### 5.5 Switching Between Chip-Select Lines

When a command targets a chip-select identifier different from the one used by the immediately preceding transaction or segment, the module shall perform a chip-select switch sequence.

The switch sequence shall ensure that:

- If the old chip-select line is still low, it is held low for the old device’s required trail time, then raised high.
- All chip-select lines are held high for an idle interval that satisfies the new device’s configured idle time.
- The new chip-select line is then asserted low.
- The new device’s configured lead time is applied before serial clocking begins.

During the switch sequence, the module shall not accept unrelated commands.

## 6. Data Transfer Control

### 6.1 TX Data Requests

For TX-only and bidirectional segments, the module shall request one byte of TX data from the data path at the start of each byte of the segment.

The TX request shall be suppressed while the module is stalled.

The module shall request exactly the number of bytes specified by the segment length.

### 6.2 RX Data Accepts

For RX-only and bidirectional segments, the module shall indicate that one received byte is complete at the end of each byte of the segment.

The RX accept shall be suppressed while the module is stalled.

The module shall indicate exactly the number of received bytes specified by the segment length.

### 6.3 Dummy Segments

For dummy segments, the module shall generate serial clock cycles without requesting TX data and without accepting RX data.

### 6.4 Bit Shift Strobes

The module shall generate shift strobes to advance the data path through the bits of each byte.

For standard speed, one bit is transferred per serial clock cycle. For dual speed, two bits are transferred per serial clock cycle. For quad speed, four bits are transferred per serial clock cycle.

The first bit of a byte is loaded as part of the byte-start strobe; subsequent bit positions are advanced by shift strobes on the appropriate serial clock edges.

Shift strobes shall be suppressed while the module is stalled.

### 6.5 Receive Sampling Strobes

The module shall generate a sampling strobe for each bit of received data, aligned to the serial clock edge on which the receiving side is expected to sample.

In normal timing mode, the sampling strobe shall occur on the sampling edge defined by the clock phase.

In full-cycle mode, the sampling strobe shall be delayed by one additional half serial clock period relative to normal timing, providing additional setup time.

Sampling strobes shall be suppressed while the module is stalled.

### 6.6 Full-Cycle Mode Indication

The module shall present the current segment’s full-cycle-mode setting to the data path so that the data path can interpret the sampling timing correctly.

### 6.7 Speed Indication

The module shall present the current segment’s speed setting to the data path so that the shift logic can select the correct number of data lines per clock cycle.

## 7. SPI Data Line Direction Control

The module shall drive the SPI data line output enables according to the current segment speed and direction.

### 7.1 Chip Select Deasserted

Whenever all chip-select outputs are deasserted high, all SPI data line drivers shall be disabled.

### 7.2 Standard Speed

In standard speed:

- The first data line is the dedicated host output line and shall be enabled whenever any chip-select output is active.
- The second data line is the dedicated receive line and shall not be enabled as an output by the host.

This applies to TX-only, RX-only, bidirectional, and dummy standard-speed segments while the chip-select line is active.

### 7.3 Dual Speed

In dual speed:

- If the segment transmits data, both of the two dual-mode data line drivers shall be enabled.
- If the segment receives data or is a dummy segment, both of the two dual-mode data line drivers shall be disabled, allowing the target device to drive the lines.

### 7.4 Quad Speed

In quad speed:

- If the segment transmits data, all four quad-mode data line drivers shall be enabled.
- If the segment receives data or is a dummy segment, all four quad-mode data line drivers shall be disabled, allowing the target device to drive the lines.

### 7.5 Direction Constraints

Bidirectional operation is only supported in standard speed. In dual and quad speeds, a segment shall be either transmitting or receiving, not both.

## 8. Stall Behavior

### 8.1 TX Stall

The module shall assert a TX stall when a TX byte is due to start but the TX data path indicates that it is not ready to provide the byte.

While a TX stall is active:

- The module shall not advance to the next byte.
- The TX byte request shall be suppressed.
- The serial clock shall hold its current level.
- The chip-select outputs shall hold their current state.
- All other data-path strobes shall be suppressed.
- No new command shall be acknowledged.

When the TX data path becomes ready, the TX request shall be issued and the transaction shall resume.

### 8.2 RX Stall

The module shall assert an RX stall when a received byte is complete but the RX data path indicates that it is not ready to accept the byte.

While an RX stall is active:

- The module shall not advance to the next byte.
- The RX accept shall be suppressed.
- The serial clock shall hold its current level.
- The chip-select outputs shall hold their current state.
- All other data-path strobes shall be suppressed.
- No new command shall be acknowledged.

When the RX data path becomes ready, the RX accept shall be issued and the transaction shall resume.

### 8.3 Simultaneous Stalls

If both TX and RX stall conditions are active, the module shall remain stalled until both conditions are resolved.

## 9. Status and Completion Indications

### 9.1 Active Status

The module shall assert the active status whenever it is not in a fully idle state.

The active status shall be asserted during:

- Lead, trail, and idle wait states.
- Chip-select switch sequences.
- Active serial clocking of a segment.

The active status shall be deasserted when:

- The module is fully idle with all chip-select lines high.
- The module is holding a chip-select line low after a chip-select-active-after-transfer segment and waiting for the next command.

### 9.2 Command-End Pulse

When the last byte of a TX-only or bidirectional segment is successfully requested from the TX data path, the module shall assert a single-cycle command-end indication.

This indication shall be qualified by TX data-path readiness and shall not be asserted during a stall.

This indication shall not be generated for RX-only or dummy segments.

## 10. Input Assumptions

The behavior of the module is specified for valid command descriptors. The command interface shall not present:

- A reserved speed value.
- A chip-select identifier greater than or equal to the number of chip-select lines.
- A bidirectional segment in dual or quad speed.

If these assumptions are violated, the module behavior is not specified.
